fullText:
Summary: Hayleys PLC (HAYL.N0000) is Sri Lanka's largest diversified group, with businesses from gloves and activated carbon to Singer, shipping and plantations. Profit is growing again: the June 2026 quarter more than doubled. At Rs 228.75 the share trades at 1.5x its NAV of Rs 148.27 and 10.8x trailing earnings. But the group's return on equity has averaged only about 11% over ten years (12.4% last year), below what an investor should demand, and it carries very heavy borrowings (about Rs 305bn, part of it funding Singer's customer credit). On that basis the methods put fair value at about Rs 138, so the price is about 66% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 117 and treat under Rs 104 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 228.75 (CSE closing price, 2026-11-06). Please check it live. In April–June 2026 it traded between Rs 214.00 and Rs 244.00. It closed the year to March 2026 at Rs 215.00, up from Rs 137.00 a year earlier and Rs 82.10 two years earlier.
Three months to 30 June 2026 (group, unaudited): revenue rose 38% to Rs 179.3bn and profit attributable to shareholders rose 137% to Rs 3.57bn. EPS was Rs 4.56 against Rs 2.01. Transport and logistics, consumer and retail (Singer) and purification (Haycarb) led the growth; the textiles and leisure businesses earned less.
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 585.0bn (up 19%), profit attributable Rs 14.05bn (up 4%), EPS Rs 18.71 (Rs 17.91), return on average equity 12.4%, NAV Rs 150.95, dividends Rs 6.00 (32% of profit). That year included a Rs 1.23bn loss from the Maldives hotel, which has since been sold.
Rights issue: 3 new shares for every 50 held raised Rs 9.0bn; the 45mn new shares were allotted on 27 April 2026, giving 795mn shares.
Debt: borrowings of about Rs 305bn against equity of Rs 177bn (including minority interests) at June 2026, with Rs 59bn of cash and deposits. Interest cover was 2.9x last year. Part of the borrowing funds Singer's hire-purchase customers and finance company.
History: EPS (after the 2023 10-for-1 split) was Rs 0.35 (2018/19), Rs 0.50 (2019/20), 10.18, 24.34, 21.80, 9.19, 17.91 and 18.71 (2025/26). ROE averaged about 11% over ten years and about 16% over the last five.

Methods
NAV (Rs 148.27): 1.5x.
Return on equity: 12.4% in 2025/26 and 14.4% in 2024/25; 8.6% in 2023/24 and under 3% in 2017–2020.
P/E: 10.8x trailing EPS of Rs 21.26. Year-end P/E: 11.5x (2026), 7.7x (2025).
Dividends: Rs 6.00 a year for the last two years, a 2.6% yield, about a third of profit.
Justified price to book: Rs 59.3 / 111.2 / 185.3, weighted Rs 110.5.
P/E method: Rs 136.0 / 200.0 / 276.0, weighted Rs 196.0.
Residual income: Rs 55.8 / 105.6 / 191.1, weighted Rs 107.8.

Hayleys pays out about a third of its profit, so a dividend model understates it, and its group cash flow is swamped by working capital and Singer's lending, so a cash-flow DCF isn't reliable. The book-based methods are much stricter than the P/E method because the group's ROE is below the cost of equity. I haven't done a sum of the parts using the market prices of its listed subsidiaries (Dipped Products, Haycarb, Singer, Alumex and others), which could give a higher figure.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 17.5% / 16% / 15% (a diversified but highly geared group).
Long-run ROE: 10% / 13.5% / 17%.
ROE path (residual income): 12% falling to 10% / 14% falling to 13.5% / 16% rising to 17%.
Long-term growth: 5% / 6% / 7%.
EPS for the year to March 2027 × P/E: 17 × 8 / 20 × 10 / 23 × 12.
Average of the three methods: Rs 83.7 / Rs 138.9 / Rs 217.5.
Common: Sri Lankan 7–10-year government bonds yield about 11–12% (the interim report quotes 10.75–10.98% for comparable government securities at June 2026). Payout 32%. Per-share figures use 795mn shares.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 138 (0.9x NAV), so Rs 228.75 is about 66% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 117.30, and 25% gives Rs 103.50.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 138.00, 150 at up to Rs 117.30 and 150 at up to Rs 103.50. That averages about Rs 121.44, about Rs 60,720, against Rs 114,375 at Rs 228.75.
Realism: Rs 138 needs about a 40% fall. The share was Rs 137 in March 2025, so it was there recently, but after a strong rise it would take a market fall or a profit setback.

Sensitivity (residual income base case, Rs per share)
Cost of equity 15%: 61.7 / 118.1 / 195.2 for long-run ROE of 10% / 13.5% / 17%.
Cost of equity 16%: 55.0 / 103.3 / 169.1.
Cost of equity 17.5%: 47.1 / 86.4 / 139.4.
Today's price needs ROE of about 17% or more for many years.

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: ROE staying above 15% (the June quarter annualises to about 12–13% on the larger equity); borrowings falling; lower interest rates, which help a group this geared; selling weaker businesses, as with the Maldives hotel; a sum of the parts showing listed subsidiaries worth well above book.
Supports a lower value: a global slowdown hitting gloves, carbon and textiles exports; a stronger rupee cutting export profits; rising interest rates; bad debts at Singer; more one-off losses.

These are my estimates from the annual reports for the years to March 2025 and March 2026 and the interim reports to June 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
